entries.claim: Modeled FY 2026-27 result: with the Budget 2025-widened new-regime slabs + 87A to 12L + 75k standard deduction, the NEW regime is cheaper than the old regime up to ~45L of income even with a full ~5L old-regime stack (80C 1.5L + 80CCD(1B) 0.5L + 24(b) 2L + 80D 1L); the old regime can only win with larger relative deductions (heavy 80D + 80E + top bands with surcharge). Verified by the deductionShieldFY27() unit-test scan.
entries.notes: Model excludes surcharge + 4% cess above 50L - the regime flip for >50L earners must be re-checked including surcharge. Re-verify at each Finance Act because any new-regime slab change flips the boundary.

entries.notes: Secondary reading (Altportfunds / Treelife 2026); confirm the specific fund tax note and the exact current-year rate before advising on a Cat III sleeve.

entries.claim: Modeled FY 2026-27 finding: with the widened new-regime slabs + 87A-to-12L, the NEW regime is cheaper for a retiree at typical income levels (below ~Rs 20L) even after giving up 80TTB/80D; even a full old-regime stack (80C 1.5L + 24b 2L + 80D 50k + 80TTB 50k = ~4.55L) does not flip the decision up to ~Rs 1 Cr in the base-slab model. The stale 'old regime wins for retirees' advice no longer holds below ~Rs 20L.
entries.notes: Base-slab model excludes surcharge; the new regime 25% surcharge cap vs the old 37% would only widen the new regime advantage at the very top. Re-verify at each Finance Act - any old-regime top-band change would flip this back.

entries.claim: NRI Section 195 TDS is a flat 30% (+surcharge +4% cess) with no exemption slabs (head rates: NRO/rent 30%, 111A 20%, 112A 12.5% above 1.25L, property LTCG 12.5% no indexation, property STCG 30%, dividends 20%); property sale TDS is on the full value (use 197 to fix); DTAA relief = TRC + Form 10F + Form 67 at the lower of domestic and treaty rate; 15G/15H unavailable to NRIs; 87A rebate NOT available to NRIs
entries.notes: The 195 head rates and the 87A/15G-15H positions are as of the FY 2026-27 transition under the Income-tax Act 2025; the individual residency day counts were unchanged. Re-verify the 195 head rates and the 87A position at each Finance Act, and confirm the specific DTAA treaty rate against the treaty text.

entries.claim: Section 54EC reinvestment is capped at Rs 50,00,000 and must be into government-notified infrastructure bonds (NHAI / REC / PFC / IRFC etc.) within 6 months of the sale; the notified-bond list is refreshed quarterly and a tranche must be open to invest
entries.notes: The 50L cap and the 6-month window are stable; the specific notified-bond issuers and tranche dates are re-notified each quarter - confirm the open tranche before acting. Re-verify the 12.5% no-indexation base and the 1-yr / 2-yr holding periods at each Finance Act.

entries.claim: Typical DTAA corridor rates FY 2026-27: DE/NL/JP/FR 10%, US/UK/AU/CA/SG ~15%, UAE 12.5% interest / 10% dividends (exemption method) vs domestic fallback 30% interest / 20% dividends; most treaties do NOT reduce capital-gains tax on Indian shares / property; Form 10F renamed Form 41 under the Income-tax Act 2025; surcharge + 4% cess still ride on the treaty base rate
entries.notes: Corridor headline rates are stable but specific treaty texts (holding conditions, MLI Principal Purpose Test, the exact 10%/15% dividend threshold) shift at each treaty ratification - re-verify the corridor table against the Income-tax Department country-wise withholding chart at review time. The 54EC/12.5% no-indexation base and the 112A threshold also ride the Finance Act cycle.

entries.claim: 80-IAC deferral window extended from 48 to 60 months for shares allotted on/after 1 Apr 2026; TDS section migrates 192->392 under Income-tax Act 2025; FAST-DS disclosure deadline 31 Dec 2026; Schedule FA penalty Rs 10L/year under Black Money Act s.43

entries.topic: Capital ladder: the four SEBI rung thresholds that unlock SIF (Rs 10L, PAN-level, MF Regs 2026, 1 Apr 2026), PMS/PRIM + AIF-employee (Rs 25L, PM Regs 2026, 1 Apr 2027), standard PMS (Rs 50L, also the 54EC cap), AIF (Rs 1Cr HNI); plus the FY 2026-27 new-regime surcharge tiers (10% > 50L, 15% > 1Cr, 25% cap > 2Cr).

54EC operational structure: the 6-month investment window, the 5-year lock-in, the Rs 50L reinvestment cap, the 12.5% no-indexation LTCG base, the REC/PFC/HUDCO/IRFC notified-bond list with ~6.5-7.5% coupons (slab-taxed), and the early-redemption reversal (exemption withdrawn, original gain re-taxed at 12.5%).

GIFT City IFSC fund tax treatment: two positions exist in FY 2026-27 (Indian-side 12.5% LTCG/slab STCG + Schedule FA vs fund-level post-tax NAV with no separate investor-side CG compute); the offer document decides. Plus the AY 2026-27 Section 50AA debt-test redefinition (non-specified int'l FoFs can now get 12.5% LTCG, not forever-slab), the ₹10L TCS-free LRS threshold, the 20% investment-remittance TCS, and the live GIFT City fund list (PPFAS S&P 500 FoF, PPFAS Nasdaq 100 FoF, DSP GIFT City Global Equity Fund, Tata GIFT City Fund).

GIFT City live scheme table (2026): PPFAS S&P 500 FoF (0.30% scheme / ~0.35% all-in, USD 5,000 min, ~USD 19.6Mn AUM, NFO 20 Mar 2026), PPFAS Nasdaq 100 FoF (0.30% / ~0.60% all-in, ~USD 9.4Mn AUM, May 2026), DSP Global Equity Fund (up to ~1.75% all-in, actively managed, ~USD 56.3Mn AUM, launched 22 Sep 2025), newly-launched Edelweiss Greater China + Marcellus Global Equities, HDFC Developed/Emerging Markets passive in pipeline; INBOUND distinction: Tata India Dynamic Equity (GIFT City) invests domestic equity at a USD 500 NRI ticket, ~2.5% all-in TER, NOT an outbound global sleeve. Resolves the Wave 22 tax-treatment conflict on the DSP primary anchor (fund-level 14.95% LTCG / 42.74% STCG, no investor-side CG, no TDS, no Schedule FA; offer document is the per-scheme tie-breaker).

Direct LRS US-equity filing layers (FY 2026-27): the 5-layer structure (1 dividend at slab + the 25% individual US dividend withholding via W-8BEN credited through Form 67, 2 the foreign-unlisted-security CG at 12.5% no-indexation LTCG after 24 months with NO pool or slab STCG, 3 the 20% TCS on the LRS investment remittance above the Rs 10L threshold as a recoverable credit, 4 Schedule FA every year with no minimum threshold, 5 the FAST-DS 2026 small-taxpayer window ~15 Aug to 31 Dec 2026 as the separate amnesty layer).

FAST-DS 2026 (Foreign Assets of Small Taxpayers - Disclosure Scheme, Finance Act 2026 Ch. IV ss.130-144, Rules notified 15 Aug 2026): the one-time window 16 Aug to 31 Dec 2026, reference date 31 Mar 2026, two categories (A = undisclosed foreign asset/income up to Rs 1 cr at 30% tax + an equal additional amount = 60% of value; B = a specified foreign asset up to Rs 5 cr that was already taxed elsewhere / acquired during non-residence but omitted from Schedule FA, at a flat Rs 1,00,000 fee), the Form 1 -> 2 -> payment -> 3/4 online sequence before the Principal DGIT (Systems), the Black Money Act immunity (asset-specific, excluding proceeds-of-crime and completed-BMA-assessment years) and the ongoing Schedule FA obligation that FAST-DS does NOT replace. The window is time-boxed - re-verify at the FY 2027-28 Budget whether it closed on 31 Dec 2026 and whether a successor scheme is announced.

Black Money Act 2015 counterfactual exposure for an undisclosed foreign asset that is neither FAST-DS-regularised nor Schedule-FA-disclosed: Section 40 (30% tax on the value) + Section 41 (a penalty of 3x the tax = 90% of value, a 120% total) + Sections 43/44 (a flat Rs 10,00,000 per defaulting assessment year for the Schedule FA omission), softened ONLY for a non-immovable asset at or under the Finance Act 2026 Rs 20L threshold (the flat penalty is waived, the 120% is not). The per-year flat-penalty stacking makes time the enemy; the ITAT Special Bench (Mr. Vinil Venugopal & Mrs. Ranjeeta Vinil) read the Section 43 "may" word as directory, not mandatory. This counterfactual is the "do nothing" column the FAST-DS 2026 defined-cost routes (60% Category A / flat Rs 1L Category B) exist to replace.
